drafts.draft_en:
2D to 3D, one character, zero modeling.

I took a flat concept sketch, generated a full turnaround, then dropped it into a moving shot with real camera parallax.

This is the step that turns AI art into AI VFX 👇
drafts.video_tip: 10-12s: 2s on the flat 2D sketch, hard cut to a 3s 360° turnaround, then a 5s shot of the character inside a scene with a slow orbit camera. Split-screen 'sketch | final' on the last frame.

drafts.draft_en:
Stop spamming credits on 40 video gens to get one usable shot.

Block the scene in 3D first: camera path, lens, lighting. Then let the video model paint over it.

Same shot, 3 gens instead of 40. VFX people have worked this way forever.
drafts.video_tip: 15s: left half shows the grey 3D blockout with the camera move, right half shows the final render in sync. End with a counter graphic '40 gens → 3 gens'.

drafts.draft_en:
Seedance 2.5 or Higgsfield for VFX shots?

I ran the same destruction plate through both. Same prompt, same seed image, same camera move.

One held the debris physics. One didn't. Guess which 👇
drafts.video_tip: 12s: A/B split of the same destruction shot, labels hidden for the first 8s, reveal model names at the end to drive guesses in replies.

drafts.draft_en:
Glass is the hardest material for AI video.

Refraction, caustics, prismatic edges. Most models melt it.

Here's the prompt structure I use to keep glass sharp across a full camera move (free prompt below) 👇
drafts.video_tip: 8-10s macro push-in on a glass object shattering in slow motion, light passing through it. Keep the background dark so the refraction pops on mobile.

drafts.draft_en:
Saturday Challenge: take one 2D character and bring it to life in 3D.

Sketch to turnaround to a 5-second shot. Any tool.

Post yours below. I'll repost my favorites tomorrow 🎬
drafts.video_tip: 10s example: your own sketch morphing into a 3D turnaround, then a short animated beat. Overlay the challenge rules as 3 short text cards.
